name: RadioVeRVe
founders: Kaustubh Srikanth (per Wikipedia; the same page also credits Gaurav Vaz and Shreyas Srinivasan with running it)
short_description: Defunct Bengaluru internet radio station that played only independent Indian music, launched on 1 June 2006.
notes: Defunct, and not electronic-focused. Useful as scene history for Indian independent online radio. Founder credit is inconsistent on the source page.

name: Be The Change Radio (BC Radio)
short_description: Online station for music by Indian bands, run by students from IIT Bombay in Mumbai.
notes: Article is dated 9 July 2012 and says it goes live 15 July, but a photo caption says it launched in 2013. Likely defunct, not confirmed. Not electronic-focused.

name: Radio Flote
short_description: Online radio station that launched the IndiEarth channel of independent music on 4 July 2013.
notes: The source does not give a city or say whether it still runs. Country is inferred from the India-focused IndiEarth channel. Verify before publishing.

name: IndiEarth
short_description: Business-to-business site and blog connecting India's non-mainstream musicians and filmmakers with media outside India, run as an EarthSync initiative.
notes: Footer credits EarthSync India Private Limited. City not stated. Source is a 2013 post, so current status is unknown.

name: Karachi Community Radio (KCR)
short_description: Karachi online community radio and production studio that promotes the local scene through artist introductions, live streams and events.
notes: Mixmag piece adds that its attached studio offers AV, virtual production and projection mapping services. Official site and handle not opened; find them before publishing.

name: Mandala Radio Nepal
short_description: Official radio platform of Mandala DJ Academy in Kathmandu, hosted on Mixcloud, with DJ mixes, live recordings and student showcases.
notes: Mixcloud page is the only source opened. Mixcloud URL is https://www.mixcloud.com/mandalaradionepal/ and plays on the page.

name: Mandala DJ Academy
short_description: Kathmandu DJ academy that runs Mandala Radio Nepal as its official radio platform.
notes: Only evidence is the Mixcloud description of the radio. No page for the academy itself was opened. Needs its own source.

name: Mixmag Asia
short_description: Asia edition of Mixmag, announced in September 2014 with an office in Bangkok, with regular India coverage, exclusive mixes and the Mixmag Asia Selects compilations.
notes: Out of strict geographic scope (Bangkok HQ per Wild City, 2014). Included because it covers India and South Asia. Mixmag Asia Radio exclusive mixes feature Indian artists, for example Farhan Rehman, dreamstates and Aaguu. Mixmag Asia Selects Volume 1 (August 2021) includes Todh Teri.

name: The Lab India (Mixmag x Budweiser BUDX)
short_description: Mixmag's live-streamed showcase series, run with Budweiser, with Indian editions in Mumbai and at DGTL Bengaluru.
notes: Wild City (23 Jan 2020) says the series launched in 2019 with weekly streamed parties at antiSOCIAL in Mumbai. Mixmag also announced a 2024 return (The Lab India returns in 2024). Videos sit on Mixmag channels.

name: Boiler Room India
short_description: Boiler Room's India editions, with streamed events in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi and Hyderabad.
notes: Boiler Room is a London company, so this is an event series in India, not an Indian body. Wild City (4 May 2022) lists Bengaluru 26 May, Mumbai 28 May, Hyderabad 29 May as a return to India, and Rolling Stone India covers the Mumbai debut. Earlier Delhi and Bangalore editions appear in Wild City headlines. Exact years of earlier editions not opened.

name: Red Bull Music Academy (India activity)
short_description: Red Bull Music Academy ran workshops, a Bass Camp in Mumbai and the RBMA Home Grown nine-city tour in India from 2011; Red Bull later shut the RBMA series.
notes: Home Grown tour ran 25 Nov to 10 Dec 2011 across nine cities (Wild City, 23 Nov 2011). RBMA is a global Red Bull program, so this is its India activity. Wild City's directory notes the shutdown but gives no year. Indian selectees include The Sine Painter (RBMA 2015) per Wild City. The 2011 start year is the earliest India activity found, not a confirmed first.

name: Selector Pro (British Council India)
short_description: British Council India program with Music Works workshops and a Visual Music residency for emerging producers and musicians.
notes: Rolling Stone India names trainers Nainita Desai, Tejas Nair (Spryk) and Avinash Kumar (BLOT!). Coven Code members met at a Selector Pro: Women in Electronic Music workshop in March 2018 per Eshe. No city or dates in the Rolling Stone piece. Funder is the British Council.

name: South Asian Music Residency (SAMUR)
short_description: Two-week residency for musicians and composers organised by Goethe-Institut Max Mueller Bhavan Chennai and K M Music Conservatory; the third edition ran 18 August to 1 September 2019.
notes: Experimental and improvised rather than club music. Directors named: Roger Hanschel and Ramesh Shotham. No funder named on the page. Later editions not checked.

name: Deccan Alternative Music Conference (DeccanAlt)
short_description: Boutique music business conference hosted by Bengaluru consultancy Neon Culture; first edition on 9 and 10 February 2024 at Bangalore Creative Circus.
notes: Founders are credited on the Ticket Fairy page; it is not fully clear whether they are founders of the conference or of Neon Culture. The second edition moved to Kochi per Music Plus headline (not opened).

name: India International Music Week (IIMW)
short_description: Five-day music trade conference and showcase festival in Goa, run by India Music Exchange, announced for February 2025.
notes: Rolling Stone India names India Music Exchange as the founder company, no individuals. Wild City also lists IIMW with DeccanAlt for Goa and Kochi showcases. Whether it ran as planned is not confirmed.

name: Ballantine's True Music Fund (India)
short_description: Fund listed by shesaid.so that backed the Boxout.fm project On Air, Online, Onward to rebuild a radio studio and daily show.
notes: Page only describes the Boxout.fm project as supported by Ballantine's True Music Fund x shesaid.so. It does not say who operates the fund or confirm an Indian programme. Treat as a funder link for Boxout.fm only until better sourced.

name: Homegrown
short_description: Indian digital media publication and content studio covering youth culture and music, with a music showcase series and the Homegrown Festival.
notes: About page names Varun and Varsha Patra as a sister and brother duo and does not give a city or founding year. It also runs HG Music and has run music showcases at The Humming Tree. Contact via homegrown.co.in/contact-us (no email on the page).

name: Rolling Stone India
short_description: Indian edition of Rolling Stone, launched on 27 February 2008 by Mumbai-based MW.Com India Pvt Ltd under licence from Wenner Media.
notes: Exchange4media names N Radhakrishnan as Editor and Publisher and Anuradha Mahindra as Editor-in-Chief at launch. Current ownership not checked.

name: Rock Street Journal (RSJ)
short_description: Monthly magazine on India and South Asia's rock scene, started in Allahabad in January 1993 and now published from Delhi, which also runs festivals.
notes: Rock-focused but RSJ has run features on Indian bass music. The Wikipedia page says it organises the Great Indian Rock Festival. Founding credit per Wikipedia intro.

name: The Indian Music Diaries (TIMD)
short_description: Indian independent music publication with news, reviews and industry features that runs the TIMD Awards, with its fifth edition in 2024.
notes: Site footer credits Inmudi Private Limited. Founders, city and founding year not stated on pages opened. It also publishes studio and music-school guides and covers Magnetic Fields lineups.

name: Mosiki
short_description: Karachi music blog run by Abdul-Rehman Malik, described by DJ Mag as Pakistan's only true alternative music blog.
notes: Single source, no founding year, current status unknown.

name: Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS)
short_description: Copyright society for composers, lyricists and music publishers in India, registered under Section 33 of the Copyright Act in 1996 and re-registered after a 2013 lapse.
notes: Founded year 1969 is inferred from a CISAC quote about its 51st year of operation in 2020 (Media Infoline) and is not stated directly, so treat as approximate. Registered as a copyright society in 1996, de-registered June 2013, later re-registered (S.S. Rana article). CEO named as Rakesh Nigam. HQ not stated on pages opened. Licenses music and lyrics (musical works), not sound recordings.

name: Phonographic Performance Limited (PPL India)
short_description: Performing rights organisation that licenses members' sound recordings for public performance and broadcast in India, founded in 1941.
notes: About page says it licenses hotels, bars, shops and radio and describes itself as no-profit, no-loss. The email on the page is partly obscured so no booking_email recorded. HQ city not stated on the page. Music Business Worldwide covers its reinstatement as a copyright society after a 12-year absence (not opened in full).

name: Indian Singers' Rights Association (ISRA)
short_description: Registered copyright society for performers formed after the 2012 Copyright Amendment to assert singers' rights alongside IPRS and PPL.
notes: SpicyIP (2018) reports FY2016-17 income of Rs 88.21 lakh. No founding year or city stated. Relevance to electronic producers is limited (performer rights).

name: Novex Communications
short_description: Company that collects public performance royalties for select labels such as Yash Raj Films and Tips while acting as their agent, not as a registered copyright society.
notes: Described in a 2018 SpicyIP piece. The 2025 to 2026 S.S. Rana article on licensing rulings was found in search but not opened, so check current status before use. Matters to club and venue licensing.

name: Madverse Music Group
short_description: Indian music distribution, publishing and marketing company serving independent artists and labels, with a partnership with Kobalt.
notes: Kobalt release names Rohan Nesho Jain as CEO and says it supports over 150,000 independent artists and labels across India and South Asia. Release is datelined Delhi but does not state HQ. Founder and year not stated on that page.

name: Songdew
founders: Sunil Khanna (named as founder in a Loudest interview title)
short_description: Online platform where independent Indian artists share, promote and distribute music, later extended to a music TV channel.
notes: Yourstory (2013) states it had over 25,000 registered artists within a year of launch. City and launch year not stated on pages opened. The Loudest founder credit comes only from the search result title, not an opened page.

name: Lost Stories Academy
short_description: Mumbai music production and DJing school started by the duo Lost Stories, teaching electronic music since 2015 from a studio in Chembur.
notes: Courses include Music Prodigy (12 months), Music Expert (7 months), Mixing and Mastering, Ableton Live and The Next Big DJ. Email taken from the official page.

name: I Love Music Academy (ILM)
short_description: Electronic music school offering DJing, production and audio engineering courses, opened in Bengaluru in 2009 and in Delhi in 2012.
notes: Wild City 2012 says it opened in Bengaluru in 2009 and a Delhi unit on 1 April 2012, with G Arjun of Jalebee Cartel teaching production and Arjun Vagale as partner. The later Wild City guide lists it in Gurgaon. Current status not checked.

name: Global Music Institute (GMI)
short_description: Greater Noida music school founded in 2011 by brothers Aditya and Tarun Balani that teaches Ableton Live, Logic Pro X and music technology.
notes: Single source, a Wild City guide of unknown year. Verify it still operates.

name: Seamedu School of Pro-Expressionism
short_description: Pune school founded in 2008 offering sound engineering degrees and diplomas plus Ableton and Logic certificate courses.
notes: Wild City guide says it became India's first Ableton Certified Training Centre the year before publication; guide date unknown, so no year is recorded. Seamedu domain appeared in a search result but was not opened.

name: Beatworx Studio
short_description: Bengaluru studio and training space teaching DJing, production, sound design, Ableton Live, mixing and mastering.
notes: Wild City guide says it began as a creative space for the Baburo brothers of Audio Units. Single source, no year.

name: DJP Media
short_description: Bengaluru Ableton Live course provider led by certified trainer Dawn John Philip, with a three-month production and performance course.
notes: Single source. Wild City calls Philip one of the few Ableton Education Partners in the country, a claim not verified on an Ableton page.

name: The Live Room Music School
short_description: Boutique South Extension school run by two certified Ableton trainers, with a 30-session production course and an Ableton Push 2 performance course.
notes: Single source, no year. Verify it still operates.

name: The True School of Music (TSM)
short_description: Mumbai music school with DJing, production and sound engineering courses, including a DJ course run with Point Blank.
notes: Point Blank Mumbai page names TSM as the partner supplying Pioneer DJ equipment for its courses. No founding year found.

name: Themusic'scool
short_description: Bengaluru school with DJing and electronic music production courses and round-the-clock facility access.
notes: Single source of unknown year. Wild City says graduates can progress to Point Blank in London. Verify it still operates.

name: K M College of Music and Technology
short_description: Chennai college, formerly K M Music Conservatory, founded by A. R. Rahman, with music technology, electronic production and audio engineering courses.
notes: Not electronic-specific. It co-hosted the 2019 South Asian Music Residency with Goethe-Institut Chennai. No founding year found.

name: The Dharavi Dream Project (#AfterSchoolOfHipHop)
short_description: Free hip hop school for young people in Dharavi, run by Universal Music India and Qyuki Digital Media, with DJing added as a core element by 2019.
notes: Source (July 2019) says four consecutive years completed and a first DJ class of 50 students. City is inferred as Mumbai (Dharavi), not stated outright. Hip hop, so adjacent to electronic.

name: Audiokraft Studio
short_description: HSR Layout recording studio in Bengaluru for composing, recording, mixing and mastering, with a green room.
notes: Homegrown list from 8 June 2021. Prices change and the studio may have closed. Not electronic-specific.

name: Resonance Studios
short_description: Shanthi Nagar jam space and recording studio in Bengaluru offering mixing, mastering and music branding help.
notes: Homegrown list from 8 June 2021. Not electronic-specific. Check it still operates.

name: COSMA Recording Studio
short_description: Kasturi Nagar studio in Bengaluru for production, film scores, mixing and mastering, with sound design and DAW courses.
notes: The Indian Music Diaries marks its own article as outdated. Mentions remote analog mastering as an extra service. Not electronic-specific.

name: Plug 'N' Play
short_description: Chittaranjan Park studio in Delhi for composition, arranging, recording, mixing and live gig recording, founded by Advaita and Anindo Bose of Shadow and Light.
notes: Source article is marked outdated by its publisher. Band-oriented, not electronic-specific.

name: Bajaao
short_description: Online and retail music store selling instruments, DJ equipment and studio gear, with stores in Mumbai, Bengaluru and Guwahati and a Mumbai jam room.
notes: Page says it has served customers since 2005 (used as founded year, not a stated founding date). Mumbai store is on the ground floor of Hi-Tech Plaza, Andheri East. Stocks Yamaha, Fender, Roland, Korg and Pearl per the page, and has a DJ gear collection.

name: DYVe
short_description: Bengaluru jam studio in Vivek Nagar, described by Homegrown in 2021 as the city's largest at 750 sq ft, with separate amps and equipment for hosting shows.
notes: Rehearsal space. 2021 listing, may have closed. Homegrown lists a Facebook page, no Instagram.

name: Nathaniel Jams
short_description: Bengaluru jam rooms (Platypus, Walrus and a Lavelle Road room) offered by Nathaniel Ventures, with monthly rehearsal packages.
notes: Rehearsal space. 2021 listing. Rock and band oriented.

name: Bread and Jaam Room
short_description: Budget jam room on Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with tube amps, monitors and a drum kit.
notes: Rehearsal space. 2021 listing, may have closed.

name: Coven Code
short_description: Delhi collective of women and non-male DJs and producers, formed in 2018 after a Selector Pro workshop, running nights, mixes and workshops with a safer-space policy.
notes: Eshe (2019) says 19 women met at the March 2018 Selector Pro: Women in Electronic Music workshop and gave their first gig a month later; no named founders. Mixmag describes it as India's first non-male collective. Wild City has a Coven Code x Orbs Cure Labs mixtape series (Orbs Cure Labs is already in labels). Handle not opened.

name: Bhai Bhai Soundsystem
short_description: Dhaka DJ collective founded in early 2022 that runs all-night parties and gives new DJs lessons, equipment and stage time.
notes: Homegrown says they stream sets with Keep Hush. Mixmag Asia radio feature (title seen in search, not opened) covers a Sri Lanka takeover with Dots Bay House.

name: Dhaka Electronic Scene
short_description: Dhaka collective that began as a Facebook group of bedroom producers and now runs workshops and releases tracks.
notes: Mixmag gives 2012. Wild City describes a collective of 100+ Bangladeshi producers, DJs, visual artists and writers, with a Facebook page (facebook.com/dhakaelectronica) and the SoundCloud above. Wild City also reviewed its Dhaka Electronica Scene compilation. Founders not named.

name: Karachi Detour Rampage
short_description: Karachi collective formed around 2010 by bedroom producers who contacted each other and started releasing tracks; later dormant.
notes: DJ Mag says around 2010 and dormant. Founders not named. Forever South, which this scene fed into, is already in labels.

name: Reggae Rajahs
short_description: New Delhi reggae and bass sound system crew started in 2009 that describes itself as the first Jamaican-style sound system in India.
notes: Wikipedia also lists the Pressure Drop radio show (2013) and the Goa Sunsplash Festival (2016). The first-in-India line is the crew's own description per Wikipedia, so keep it attributed.

name: Bay Beat Collective
short_description: Mumbai bass music DJ collective formed in 2008 from weekly nights at Zenzi Bar, now a duo of Sohail Arora and Kris Correya.
notes: Rolling Stone India names the three founding members. Arora also runs Krunk (already in promoters) and launched Bass Camp Festival in 2010 per RSJ. Rolling Stone says the lineup was a duo at time of writing (date not shown).

name: BassFace
short_description: Pune bass music collective behind the Bass Tapri series, whose first event was in May 2026 at antiSOCIAL on FC Road.
notes: New collective with one source. Founders are given by first name only. antiSOCIAL is already in promoters as a club.

name: We All Should Play
short_description: Kathmandu cultural agency co-founded by Rishi Jha and Marta that runs the Seashells On The Mountains residency.
notes: DJ Mag describes the founders as a husband and wife team. No year or website found.

name: Sine Valley Music Festival
short_description: Festival and residency in Nepal conceived by Pakistani artist Alien Panda Jury and Maldives-based M.Manal, launched in 2016.
notes: DJ Mag says it ran two initial editions before Nepali concert funding dried up. 2016 is the year the founders decided to launch it. Status now unknown. Alien Panda Jury also started the Oscillations event series in Karachi per DJ Mag's Karachi piece.
